newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-What's Happening in Australian Sport.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-What's Happening in Australian Sport.

text.p: Australia's struggling cricketers must beat South Africa in their limited overs match in India later today to retain any hopes of qualifying for the final of the triangular tournament.
A victory is essential if Mark Taylor's men are to clinch a final berth ahead of their hosts, India.
South Africa, the most impressive team of the tournament to date, have already booked their place.
At home, the touring England A side are facing a potential difficult assignment this weekend against New South Wales 2nd XI in Tamworth.
On Saturday, West Indies arrive in Perth at the start of their five-test tour.
They will play a Chairman's XI in the traditional tour opener at Lilac Hill outside Perth on November 4.
In the domestic Mercantile Mutual limited overs competition, South Australia entertain Queensland in Adelaide on Sunday.
HORSE RACING
Several Melbourne Cup horses -- notably trainer Gai Waterhouse's best hope Nothin' Leica Dane -- will finalise their preparations in the Mackinnon Stakes over 2000 metres at Flemington on Saturday.
Irish stayer Oscar Schindler, the firm favourite to win the Cup on Tuesday, will rest this weekend.
RUGBY UNION

Australia have suffered further injury setbacks on their tour to Britain, with number eight Michael Brial and centre Jason Little sidelined by serious ankle and knee ligaments problems respectively. Second row forward Garrick Morgan has already returned home because of a broken ankle. The Australian Rugby Union has sent for back rower Owen Finegan and centre Adam Magro as cover for Brial and Little, who will stay with the tour party in the hope of recovery.
Meanwhile, Australia have named their side for the tour match against Combined Scottish Districts in Glasgow on Saturday.
The team is:

15-Joe Roff; 14-Ben Tune, 13-Daniel Herbert, 12-Pat Howard, 11-David Campese; 10-David Knox, 9-George Gregan: 8-Mark Connors, 7-David Wilson (captain), 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Welborn, 4-David Giffin, 3-Andrew Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Richard Harry.
But coach Greg Smith remains unimpressed with his side's form in the Scottish leg of their European tour following an unconvincing 47-20 win against Scotland A on Wednesday.
SOCCER
Australia national team captain Paul Wade will win his 84th and final cap against Tahiti in the return leg of the Oceania Nations Cup final in Canberra later today.
The 34-year-old Canberra Cosmos defender earlier this week announced his retirement from the international arena, ending a national team career spanning ten years.
Australia won the first leg 6-0 in Papeete last weekend and are virtually assured of progressing to the rich Confederation Cup in Saudi Arabia in December next year.
In the domestic Ericsson Cup, Marconi Fairfield take on neighbours Sydney United at home.
BASKETBALL

It's the business end of the season and South East Melbourne Magic must win the second game of the National Basketball League grand final series to prevent city neighbours Melbourne Tigers from winning the title.
The Tigers won the opening game of the best-of-three series 100-89 one week ago, with captain Andrew Gaze scoring a game-high 35 points.
The two teams will meet again in a deciding match at Melbourne Park on Sunday, if necessary.
